static_traits.name: Lin Yao
static_traits.family_status: Lives with spouse and children, has a vacation house in the mountains
static_traits.social_status: Spouse is supportive but has not yet fully understood the intensity of the Fear; Family relationships have grown tense because of unwillingness to drive
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychotherapy history; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation, strong logic; Positive attitude; Significant anxiety appearing when talking about driving, describing physiological reactions like heart palpitations, chest tightness, dizziness

basic_info.main_problem: Strong Fear of having an accident and immediate Death while driving an SUV, appearing months after purchasing the car and gradually escalating, leading to trying to Avoid driving.
basic_info.core_demands: I become aware that this fear is becoming a major obstacle to my daily life and responsibilities, so I seek counseling; I hope to regain a sense of control over the fear and restore independence.

special_situations.event: Driving an SUV on the highway
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If driving a large and powerful vehicle on the highway, once something happens it would be fatal
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to avoid highways, pulls over when necessary, reduces the number of drives
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will lose control and crash right away, possibly dying on the spot

special_situations.event: Driving in congested traffic or busy roads
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Accidents are more likely in complex road conditions; once one happens I will be unable to cope
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding rush hours and complex road sections, reducing travel
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Traffic is so complicated; an accident will soon happen to me

special_situations.event: Holding the SUV steering wheel, feeling the vehicle's size and power
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The bigger and more powerful the vehicle, the harder it is for me to control; mistakes would have serious consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Drives tensely and stiffly, uses breathing and distraction techniques to relieve it, but still tends to avoid
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This car is too big and too powerful; I simply cannot control it

special_situations.event: Hears or thinks of news about a similar SUV having an accident
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: This type of vehicle is more dangerous; I am also very likely to have the same accident
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reinforcing avoidance of driving, using danger information as the reason for not driving
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Driving an SUV makes accidents more likely

core_conflict.wish: Longs for safety and controllability, to be able to drive with peace of mind and maintain life independence
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of losing control and fatal accidents
defense_goal: Reducing the sense of danger and Anxiety by Avoiding driving, maintaining subjective safety

object_relations.self_representation: A vulnerable driver prone to losing control
object_relations.object_representation: The spouse is a supporter but an onlooker who has not yet fully understood the Fear

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the source of the fear or needing to explain why one fears driving SUVs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to attribute fear entirely to the vehicle's objective size and power, regarding it as the main source of danger
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using objective, rational statements to emphasize the vehicle's 'size and power', downplaying subjective feelings; steady tone, systematically Interpreting risks, reducing emotional exposure.

manifestations: Strongly imagines a fatal accident while driving an SUV
Stronger DeathFear in high-speed and busy road conditions
Accompanied by physical reactions such as heart palpitations, chest tightness, dizziness

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: Not yet fully expressing the Fear's intensity and impact to the spouse, choosing to bear it alone
Prefers self-regulation (breathing, distraction) over proactively seeking external support

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse and family resources
Objective evidence that most driving experiences were actually safe without accidents
Positive attitude, willing to try gradual practice to rebuild a sense of control
negative_force: Cognitive patterns of catastrophizing and predicting the future
Control fallacy about large vehicles (believing oneself unable to control them)
Avoiding driving leading to functional limitation and maintaining the Fear
Not yet fully expressing Fear intensity to family, finding it hard to obtain effective support

antecedent: Every time getting in the SUV to drive after buying it
target_behavior.core_reason: Dangerous feelings about vehicle size and power triggering catastrophizing and predicting-the-future thinking, worrying about losing control and fatal accidents
target_behavior.function: Avoids fear and subjective danger, gains immediate security
target_behavior.consequence: Daily activities and Independence limited; Family relationships growing tense

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Anxiety/panic reactions while driving (heart palpitations, chest tightness, dizziness, trembling)
antecedent: When driving an SUV on highways or in congested traffic
The automatic thought 'I will lose control and have a fatal accident' appears
target_behavior.core_reason: Emotional reasoning and catastrophizing amplify the subjective experience of danger, forming a conditioned physiological stress response
target_behavior.function: Prompts stopping or reducing driving through physiological reactions to avoid perceived danger
target_behavior.consequence: Needing to pull over or interrupt driving, further reinforcing the avoidance cycle
